items.followUp: State two roles of magnesium in plant life.

rubric.why: Iron is needed for chlorophyll formation, although it is not part of the chlorophyll molecule.
rubric.description: Explains iron's role in chlorophyll formation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that iron is needed to make chlorophyll but is not a constituent of it.

rubric.why: Iron is also present in cytochromes involved in electron transport.
rubric.description: States another role of iron in plants.
rubric.how: Award for identifying cytochromes or their role in electron transport.

modelAnswer: Iron is required for the formation of chlorophyll, although it is not a constituent of the chlorophyll molecule.
Iron is a component of cytochromes, which take part in electron transport during respiration and photosynthesis.

items.followUp: Name four environmental factors that affect the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Light affects stomatal opening and therefore transpiration.
rubric.how: Award for naming light or light intensity.

rubric.why: Temperature influences evaporation from leaf surfaces.
rubric.how: Award for naming temperature.

rubric.why: Humidity affects the water-vapour gradient between the leaf and the air.
rubric.how: Award for naming humidity.

rubric.why: Wind or air movement removes moist air from around the leaf.
rubric.description: Identifies wind or air movement as a factor.
rubric.how: Award for naming wind or air movement.

modelAnswer: The rate of transpiration is affected by light intensity, temperature, humidity and wind or air movement.
Soil-water availability and the number of stomata can also affect the rate.

items.followUp: Describe five differences between plant cells and animal cells.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus, unlike eukaryotic cells.
rubric.how: Award for correctly contrasting the absence of a true nucleus in prokaryotes with its presence in eukaryotes.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular, whereas eukaryotic chromosomes are linear.
rubric.description: Compares the form of genetic material.
rubric.how: Award for correctly giving circular DNA in prokaryotes and linear DNA in eukaryotes.

rubric.why: The two cell types characteristically have different ribosome sizes.
rubric.how: Award for correctly stating 70S ribosomes in prokaryotes and 80S ribosomes in eukaryotes.

rubric.why: Membrane-bound organelles are absent from prokaryotes and present in eukaryotes.
rubric.how: Award for a correct contrast, such as the presence of mitochondria in eukaryotes but not prokaryotes.

rubric.why: Prokaryotes divide by binary fission, whereas eukaryotic cells divide by mitosis or meiosis.
rubric.how: Award for correctly contrasting binary fission with mitosis or meiosis.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus; eukaryotic cells have a nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.
Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular; eukaryotic chromosomes are linear.
Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes; eukaryotic cells have 80S ribosomes in their cytoplasm.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have them, for example mitochondria.
Prokaryotic cells divide by binary fission; eukaryotic cells divide by mitosis or meiosis.

items.followUp: Define photosynthesis, write its equation and outline the three stages of the Calvin cycle.

rubric.why: The definition must describe the production of food from carbon dioxide and water using light energy.
rubric.how: Award for describing the use of light energy to make glucose or food from carbon dioxide and water.

rubric.why: The balanced equation represents the reactants and products of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for the balanced equation with carbon dioxide and water yielding glucose and oxygen.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide is fixed to RuBP to form PGA.
rubric.description: Describes carbon fixation in the dark reactions.
rubric.how: Award for stating that CO₂ combines with RuBP to form PGA.

rubric.why: PGA is reduced to PGAL using energy and reducing power.
rubric.how: Award for stating that PGA is reduced to PGAL using ATP and NADPH.

rubric.why: Some PGAL can form sugars, while the rest is used to regenerate RuBP.
rubric.description: Describes sugar formation and regeneration of the CO₂ acceptor.
rubric.how: Award for stating that PGAL forms sugar and/or regenerates RuBP.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O  —light and chlorophyll→  C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
Carbon fixation: CO₂ combines with RuBP to form PGA.
Reduction: PGA is reduced to PGAL using ATP and NADPH.
Regeneration: Some PGAL is used to make sugars, while the remaining PGAL regenerates RuBP.

rubric.why: Enzymes are protein molecules.
rubric.description: States the chemical nature of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award for identifying enzymes as proteins.

rubric.why: Enzymes catalyse biochemical reactions.
rubric.description: States that enzymes act as catalysts.
rubric.how: Award for saying enzymes speed up or catalyse reactions.

rubric.why: An enzyme generally acts on a particular substrate or reaction.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that enzymes are specific to their substrates or reactions.

rubric.why: Enzyme activity is affected by environmental conditions such as temperature and pH.
rubric.description: States that enzyme activity depends on conditions.
rubric.how: Award for noting an optimum temperature or pH, or that changes in these conditions affect activity.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts and speed up biochemical reactions.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzymes are not used up during reactions and can be reused.
Their activity is affected by temperature and pH; each enzyme works best at an optimum temperature and pH.

items.followUp: Write a note on vitamin D, including its function and deficiency disease.

rubric.why: Ascorbic acid is the chemical name for vitamin C.
rubric.description: Identifies ascorbic acid as vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award for naming vitamin C or ascorbic acid.

rubric.why: Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as water soluble.

rubric.why: Vitamin C helps form collagen and supports healthy gums and wound healing.
rubric.description: Gives a function of vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award for a valid function, such as collagen formation or maintaining healthy gums.

rubric.why: A deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy.
rubric.how: Award for naming scurvy.

modelAnswer: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, a water-soluble vitamin found in citrus fruits and other fresh fruits and vegetables.
It is needed for collagen formation, wound healing and healthy gums.
A deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy, which may involve bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

items.followUp: What are the major bioelements, and name four elements found in living organisms?

rubric.why: Bioelements are the elements present in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that bioelements are elements present in living organisms.

rubric.why: Examples demonstrate understanding of which elements are bioelements.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least two valid examples, such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen or nitrogen.

modelAnswer: Bioelements are the elements that are present in living organisms.
Examples include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.

items.followUp: Define the ecosystem level of biological organization.

rubric.why: The biosphere is the part or zone of Earth where life exists.
rubric.description: Identifies the biosphere as Earth's life-supporting zone.
rubric.how: Award for describing it as the part of Earth where organisms live.

rubric.why: The biosphere includes all ecosystems on Earth.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it includes all Earth's ecosystems.

modelAnswer: The biosphere is the part of Earth where life exists.
It includes all the ecosystems on Earth and is the highest level of biological organization.
